claude.sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

links.outcome: Concordance and safety of LLM recommendations with vs without in-context guideline grounding (non-equivalent comparison)
links.effect: Guideline-integrated Gemini 2.5: kappa 0.792, exact concordance 85.0%, safe 83.7%; MedGemma without guidelines: kappa 0.566-0.610, safe 62.3-62.7% (p<0.001). Confounded by model differences.
links.quote: Guideline-integrated general-purpose LLMs, exemplified by Gemini 2.5, demonstrated higher concordance with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions compared with a domain-specialized model without external retrieval.

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety of LLM treatment recommendations against MTB reference standard with blinded expert adjudication
links.effect: Gemini 2.5 safe in 83.7% of cases; MedGemma 62.3% (T=0) and 62.7% (T=1); weighted kappa 0.792 vs 0.566/0.610.
links.quote: In the safety assessment, Gemini 2.5 demonstrated the highest proportion of safe recommendations (83.7%), whereas MedGemma (T = 0.0: 62.3% and T = 1.0: 62.7%) showed higher rates of potentially risky and harmful recommendations.

links.outcome: LLM concordance with current guideline-based tumor board decisions in complex clinical scenarios
links.effect: Discordance concentrated in surgical/interventional planning, active surveillance, recurrent disease, stage IV and poor performance status; MedGemma concordance for surgery 11.1-22.2%, surveillance 39.3-44.0%.
links.quote: The lowest concordance rates for both temperature settings were observed in active surveillance (39.3% for T = 0.0 and 44.0% for T = 1.0) and surgical/interventional procedures (11.1% and 22.2%, respectively).

links.outcome: Comparison of two candidate LLMs against tumor board decisions on the same cases
links.effect: Gemini 2.5 (guideline-integrated) outperformed MedGemma 27B on concordance and safety (p<0.001); full concordance 81.7% vs 57.0% (T=0) and 62.3% (T=1).
links.quote: Comparisons of the three-category concordance distributions showed significant differences between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 0.0) ( p < 0.001) and between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 1.0) ( p < 0.001).

links.outcome: LLM concordance across patient subgroups (sex, age, comorbidity, ECOG, stage, MSI)
links.effect: Gemini concordance did not differ by sex, age, comorbidity, ECOG, location or MSI (p>0.05) but differed by TNM stage, setting and modality; MedGemma varied by stage, ECOG, MSI.
links.quote: Across demographic and clinical variables, concordance between Gemini 2.5 and MTB decisions did not differ significantly by sex, age at diagnosis, comorbidity status, ECOG performance status, tumor location, or MSI status (all p > 0.05).

links.outcome: Effect of temperature setting on MedGemma concordance and safety
links.effect: T=1.0 improved concordance vs T=0.0 (accuracy 73.5% vs 70.3%, p=0.038) but safety did not differ (62.7% vs 62.3%, p=0.567).
links.quote: These findings indicate that although increasing the temperature improved MedGemma’s concordance, it did not result in a meaningful improvement in its safety profile.

links.outcome: Concordance and safety of treatment recommendations
links.effect: Gemini guideline-integrated: κ=0.792, exact agreement 85.0%, safety 83.7%; MedGemma no retrieval: accuracy 70.3%/73.5%, safety 62.3%/62.7%.
links.quote: In this retrospective analysis of 300 colorectal cancer cases discussed at multidisciplinary tumor boards, a guideline-integrated general-purpose LLM, Gemini 2.5, demonstrated a high level of agreement with MTB treatment decisions, achieving substantial concordance (weighted Cohen’s κ = 0.792) and a high exact agreement rate (85.0%), whereas a domain-specialized model operating without external retrieval, MedGemma 27B, showed moderate concordance that improved modestly with higher temperature settings.

links.effect: Gemini safe 83.7%; MedGemma safe 62.3% (T=0.0) and 62.7% (T=1.0), with higher potentially risky/harmful rates.
links.quote: In the safety assessment, Gemini 2.5 demonstrated the highest proportion of safe recommendations (83.7%), whereas MedGemma (T = 0.0: 62.3% and T = 1.0: 62.7%) showed higher rates of potentially risky and harmful recommendations.

links.outcome: Subgroup concordance by ECOG and MSI
links.effect: MedGemma discordance was more frequent for ECOG ≥2 vs 0–1 (p=0.023/0.036) and MSI-unstable/unknown vs stable (p<0.001).
links.quote: Discordance was more frequent in patients with ECOG ≥ 2 compared with those with ECOG 0–1 (T = 0.0: p = 0.023; T = 1.0: p = 0.036), and in MSI-unstable or MSI-unknown tumors compared with MSI-stable disease ( p < 0.001 for both settings).

unlisted_practices: Testing MedGemma response-temperature settings (T = 0.0 vs T = 1.0) for oncology recommendation concordance and safety.

links.outcome: treatment recommendation concordance and clinical safety
links.effect: Gemini 2.5 (guideline-integrated) achieved 83.7% safe recommendations vs 62.3% (T=0.0) and 62.7% (T=1.0) for unaugmented MedGemma (p<0.001); full concordance was 81.7% vs 57.0% and 62.3% (p<0.001).
links.quote: In the safety assessment, Gemini 2.5 demonstrated the highest proportion of safe recommendations (83.7%), whereas MedGemma (T = 0.0: 62.3% and T = 1.0: 62.7%) showed higher rates of potentially risky and harmful recommendations.
